query: How do review themes differ between positive and negative IMDb sentiment?

per_column.name: overall_verdict_tone
per_column.rationale: A graded tone axis adds resolution beyond the binary label_pos, enabling comparison of intensity and mixed cases. Somewhat redundant with the existing label and with emotional_impact, but the mixed/mild distinctions give modest new leverage. Sample values track the source text well.

per_column.name: recommendation_stance
per_column.rationale: Explicit vs implicit recommend/discourage is a genuine thematic axis distinct from raw sentiment and useful for contrasting positive/negative reviews. Values are well grounded (e.g. 'A must see' -> explicit_recommend). The explicit/implicit split is somewhat inferential but defensible.

per_column.name: emotional_impact_on_reviewer
per_column.rationale: Largely a restatement of overall_verdict_tone/sentiment intensity, offering little new analytical axis for a theme-comparison query. Values are sound readings of the text, but the redundancy limits usefulness.

per_column.name: acting_quality_assessment
per_column.rationale: Aspect-level praised/criticised on acting directly supports comparing themes across sentiment, with appropriate NULLs when acting is unmentioned. Sample readings are accurate (row 4 praised, row 3 criticised).

per_column.name: directing_technical_quality
per_column.rationale: A distinct aspect axis useful for the query with correct NULL handling. Slightly weaker grounding: row 4 marked 'praised' rests on 'well-made', reasonable but thin; row 1 'criticised' for directing is a looser inference from a writing-focused review.

per_column.name: primary_praise_target
per_column.rationale: Categorising what a review praises is exactly the kind of theme axis the query needs, with rich, non-trivial categories and 'not_present' for silence. Sample values well grounded (row 4 -> specific_actor).

per_column.name: primary_criticism_target
per_column.rationale: Symmetric criticism-target categorisation gives strong grouping leverage for contrasting negative-review themes. Values match source (row 1/2 -> writing_script, row 3 -> acting).

per_column.name: comparison_reference_valence
per_column.rationale: Whether a review invokes favourable/unfavourable comparisons is a genuine distinct theme axis. Well grounded (row 1 references Star Trek/Voyager unfavourably; row 4 no_comparison). Slightly sparser signal than aspect columns.

judge.rationale: The added columns provide several genuinely distinct thematic axes -- recommendation stance, aspect-level praise/criticism, praise/criticism targets, and comparison valence -- that give strong grouping and contrast leverage for a positive-vs-negative theme analysis. A couple of columns (emotional_impact_on_reviewer, and to a lesser degree overall_verdict_tone) largely restate sentiment intensity and add little new. Values across the row samples are sound readings of the source text, with appropriate NULL/not_present handling for silent rows and only minor over-inference in the directing aspect. No clear hallucinations observed.
